ADR-0044 D (line 166) records the same shape for `cancelled` (「`ExecutionStatus` already reserves the value」). A spec-first member with a short producer-less window is the repo's existing way of adding a run status.

## Ruling: A

**Why not C.** The ruling's text is 「status `missed`」, and 置信门 ③ forbids overturning a maintainer ruling here. On the merits, a `cancelled` row that nobody cancelled, or a `failed` row where nothing ran, makes one stored value mean two things, and every reader of `?status=cancelled` (the approvals liveness read, the retention sweep, a run list) would carry the ambiguity from then on. The engine's own history says what that costs: #15223 found two statuses folded into `failed` and called the information 「DESTROYED at write time」.

**Why not B.** The repo at large does know a declared cross-lane spec touch with a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review (seat post #18549 carries several, e.g. `6269616435`, `6274926251`, `6346165242`). Two texts still bar it for this card: the services lane's red line 「零持有 `packages/spec`」, which `SKILL.md` puts outside the four-axis weighing, and this project owner's rule that the spec lane is another account's and this project edits nothing there. A ruling thread moves neither; lifting a red line is the owner's word, not a letter. The card's own analysis says the same (「needs an explicit release」). With A available and the hand-off channel measured to answer within hours today, nothing is gained by asking for that release.

**Why A is inside the text, and self-rulable.** The contract decision, that the run history carries `missed`, is the maintainer's; what forked is the order of two technical tasks across two lanes and the way the second verifies against the first, the named non-escalation class 「技术任务间顺序与依赖;验证策略」. A is also the only letter every governing line already prescribes: 改协议单独立卡; `packages/spec` 恒归本席; the cross-seat request rides on this card with `Blocked-by:` and one comment on the target seat; spec first, downstream blocked. No floor moves: no security or permission boundary; the published contract changes exactly as the maintainer ruled it and in the lane that owns it; no product trade-off beyond the ruled one; no gate touched. Failure is loud and reverts once: before the spec member lands, a `missed` row is refused by the column's `Field.select` and `?status=missed` answers 400 at the REST boundary; if the spec lane declines or reshapes the member, the services PR is not opened and the card comes back here as a fresh fork (item 7).

Fixed here, so the dev opens no second decision:

1. **The spec request is one comment on #18549, not a card from this project.** The card thread posts it in the same act as its `Ruling-ref:` note here, in the shape of `6349666746`: this ruling's id, the card number, the maintainer's sentence as the card quotes it, and the asked shape below. It asks the spec seat to answer on #25235 with the spec card's number (or the PR), so this card can carry `Blocked-by:`. Priority, shape and TSDoc wording are that seat's; what follows is the request as this lane reads it, not an instruction to that lane.
2. **The asked shape.** `ExecutionStatus` gains `'missed'`, appended LAST (the file's own rule for `refused`; `execution.test.ts:28-30` moves with it: the ninth stays `refused`, the tenth is `missed`, the first eight unchanged). TSDoc, in substance: a scheduled flow's due time that passed while no kernel was ticking, recorded once at the next tick that found it, cloud#3149 item 5; terminal, never started, never resumed, never replayed; DISTINCT from `cancelled` (nobody cancelled it) and from `failed` (nothing ran); on the run row and the `ExecutionLog`, `startedAt` carries the due time and `completedAt` the detection time, `durationMs` is absent (nothing ran), `error` and `refusalMessage` are absent. No new field. ⛔ Not `AutomationResult.status` or `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.status` (the five stay five; `contracts/automation-result-status.pin.test.ts` is untouched), ⛔ not `JobExecutionStatus`. `ListRunsRequestSchema.status` and the REST filter widen by construction (both read the enum); `content/docs/references/automation/execution.mdx` and `api/automation-api.mdx` regenerate. Declarations are the spec seat's to set; this lane reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` (a run-row and wire value, nothing an author writes). The member sits producer-less until item 4 lands, exactly as `refused` did between #14945 and #15788; item 4 keeps that window to one CI round by being ready when the spec PR merges.
3. **The services build proceeds now, locally.** The card thread continues under claim `6353512245` on its branch and worktree against `origin/main`. For typecheck and tests it may carry the one spec line as an UNCOMMITTED worktree edit; ⛔ that line is never committed, never pushed, and the PR's file list is verified to hold no `packages/spec/**` path. Premise for opening the PR, falsifiable: `git grep -n "'missed'" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts` hits. While it does not, no PR is opened.
4. **The services PR, one PR, `Fixes #25235`.** Surface as the claim records it (`db-job-adapter.ts`, `schedule-trigger.ts` plus one new sibling module, `engine.ts`, `sys-automation-run.object.ts`, tests in each touched package, one `patch` changeset per touched published package: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, as claimed). The three enumerations widen together in this PR (`TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, the column's options, the retention `onlyWhen` set), plus every pin that enumerates them and the approvals terminal map at `approval-service.ts:526`, found by `grep -rn "'timed_out'" packages --include='*.ts'` at the PR's base. Title under `feat(…)`, no `!` (nothing is refused that was accepted). After the spec member is on `origin/main`: merge `origin/main`, run the derived gate list on the final head, a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record is not owed by path (no spec path in the diff) unless `dispatch-gates --tier` says otherwise for the claimed paths; hand back to `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) for ACCEPT.
5. **The design, as ruled.** (a) One row per missed due time, per flow; the row id is a deterministic function of (flow name, due time) so two replicas detecting the same gap write one row; a second insert of the same id is a no-op, proven by a two-detector test. (b) No replay, no catch-up, no run; `cloud#1288` is not restarted. (c) The gap is bounded, not inferred: it starts at the newest instant a kernel is known to have touched the job (`sys_job.last_run_at`, else the row's bind time) and ends at this kernel's first tick for the flow; a due time inside it is `missed` only when the `sys_job` row is still `active` AND the `(flow, tick-window)` key has no claim in `sys_flow_dispatch`. (d) Where the engine runs with no persisted dispatch ledger (its own one-time warning 「trigger dispatch dedup is IN-PROCESS ONLY」), detection is SKIPPED with one warn line naming the flow, ⛔ never inferred from the absence of claims. (e) The bound: per flow per detection, at most `maxTerminalRunsPerFlow` (the store's configured value, default 100; ⛔ not a second literal) newest due times are written, oldest first dropped; the drop is one warn line naming the flow, the count not written and the earliest due time dropped. This is not a new product bound: the store deletes every terminal row beyond that count in the same write (`pruneFlowOverflow`), so writing more is writing rows the store removes at once. (f) `started_at` = due time, `finished_at` = detection time, `duration_ms` absent, as item 2's TSDoc says. (g) The retention sweep and the per-flow cap treat a `missed` row as any terminal row (that is what widening the `onlyWhen` set means); a flow whose kernel was off for long therefore fills its terminal history with `missed` rows and the older real runs age out of the newest-100 window. ⛔ Not ruled here and flagged for the maintainer: whether `missed` rows should be bounded TIGHTER than the store's cap so that real history survives a long outage; one word from the maintainer sets a smaller bound, and this ruling's (e) then reads that bound instead.
6. **The one premise the design stands on, and the fix if it fails.** Premise: a `sys_job` row that is still `active` at this kernel's first bind was armed by a kernel that stopped ticking, not deliberately refused. Measured false in one path at `258f4e6`: a kernel whose scheduled-work policy is OFF refuses the bind without cancelling a previous kernel's job (`start()` → `stop()` cancels only `this.bound`, `:694-700`, `:1007-1010`), so a later kernel with the policy ON would read that kernel's whole life as a gap. ⛔ Those due times are not `missed`: the platform refused them on purpose. The dev closes it inside the claimed surface, in `trigger-schedule`: the policy-OFF refusal cancels the job by its deterministic name (`JOB_PREFIX:flowName`) through the job service whether or not this process bound it, so the row is `inactive` and the detector records nothing. Pinned both ways (OFF kernel between two ON kernels: zero `missed` rows; evicted ON kernel: one row per due time). If closing it needs a `sys_job` column or any `packages/platform-objects` or `packages/spec` change, ⛔ stop and report the fork on this card; do not record and do not guess.
7. **Card state while waiting.** Once the local build is green under item 3 and the spec member is not yet on `origin/main`, the thread parks the card and frees its slot: `pm:blocked` with a line-initial `Blocked-by: #N` naming the spec card when the spec seat has answered with a number; else `pm:on-hold` with `Restart-when: git grep -n "'missed'" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts hits`, rewritten to `pm:blocked` when the number is known (the `6351169534` pattern on #25190). The branch keeps the work; the re-claim names it under `Resume-from:`. ⛔ If the spec lane declines the member or reshapes it (a different literal, a different home), nobody writes an off-spec value, nobody falls back to C, nobody carries the spec hunk (B): the card returns to the box as a fresh fork citing that answer.
8. **The reader on the other side.** At this PR's ACCEPT, `domain:services` seat 1 greps `../objectui` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` for the run-status rendering (`timed_out`, `refused` literals in the run-history and status-badge components). A closed map ⇒ one `domain:ui` card in objectui with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#25235` (cross-repo rule 3; the ui lane is this project's); a pass-through label ⇒ a line in the acceptance notes. ⛔ No objectui edit in this PR.
9. ⛔ **Not:** `packages/spec/**` in any commit of this card, `packages/platform-objects/**`, `packages/runtime/**` (the REST filter widens by reading the enum), `packages/client`, `cloud#1288`, any replay or catch-up run, any new gate or script.

### Why A, on the four axes (business standpoint)

- **① Long-term soundness (weight ≥50%).** Two years out, a flow's run history has one closed vocabulary, declared once in the spec, with `missed` meaning one thing in every reader: the Runs list, the `?status=` filter, retention, approvals liveness, and the console badge. A gets there the way the repo already added `refused` and reserved `cancelled`: the spec declares the member in its own lane, the producer and its three stored-vocabulary sites land together. B reaches the same enum through a door the lane's own charter closes; C puts two meanings on one stored value for good.
- **② Measured business pull.** The maintainer ruled it from a measured gap on the hosted kernel (cloud#3149 item 5, `clock-trigger-arming.ts`): an app that owns a daily sweep today cannot tell that the sweep did not run. cloud#3149 is `Blocked-by:` this card. The pull is real and dated; the cost of A over B is one hand-off comment and one spec PR, a channel that answered twice today within hours.
- **③ AI-error prevention.** Under A every wrong state is loud and early: a `missed` row before the member lands is refused as `invalid_option`; `?status=missed` answers 400 until the enum carries it; a degraded dispatch ledger skips detection with a warn instead of inventing gaps; a kernel that refused on purpose leaves an inactive row, not a false `missed`. Under C a reader must know which `cancelled` rows were never cancelled, the quiet direction.
- **④ Startup no-sprawl.** One enum member, no new field, no new table, no new gate; the per-flow bound reuses the store's existing cap instead of a second constant; the policy-OFF fix restores an invariant inside the claimed surface. B is the same diff in the wrong lane; C adds a permanent reading rule to every consumer instead.

Only-① pick: A. Do ②③④ flip it: no. Effort for the chosen letter: this card `M`, `effort: high`, same thread, no new slot; the spec PR is the spec seat's to size (one member, one pin, two regenerated pages); the objectui reader, if any, is a separate `domain:ui` card.
